blocks.text: Eye Safety: Proper eye protection must be worn at all times by anyone performing or observing science activities.

blocks.text: Clothing Protection: This symbol appears when substances could stain or burn clothing.
Animal Safety: This symbol appears when safety of animals and students must be ensured.
Radioactivity: This symbol appears when radioactive materials are used.
Handwashing: After the lab, wash hands with soap and water before removing goggles.

blocks.features: Plain bold caption labelling the in-text example beneath it; also excluded from the model.

uncertain: Options 1 and 2 both derive the icons' word meanings ('Eye Safety', 'Clothing Protection', 'Handwashing') from the front-of-book icon key elsewhere on the same print page, since no words are printed at the icons' own location (only icon graphics) -- the mapping is unambiguous (confirmed against the PDF page image, p.126) but is not literally print TEXT at that spot.
resolution: `illustrates.rule`/`quote` resolved to "4.9.2.a" (the specific lettered clause that names Option 1's own technique -- "icon headings may be expressed in words... a better option for earlier grades") rather than either run's "4.9.2b"/"4.9.2.b" (which is Option 2's clause, about shape codes on the Special Symbols page; see that file). `print.blocks` rebuilt directly from the PDF page image (p.126, read directly): kept run A's fuller icon-key descriptions (title+description text, not run B's title-only summary) but corrected `kind` to `other` for the whole icon-key strip and its caption (run A had tagged these `list-item`, which -- per this section's print.blocks-to-model mapping -- would incorrectly inject all five icon-key entries into the model; neither braille option ever transcribes them). `level` for "Procedure" resolved to 2 (cell-5), confirmed directly against .txt line 3778 (4 leading blank cells) -- contradicting run A's stated level 3 (cell-7).
